target_customer: Bay Area homeowners replacing gas furnaces and air conditioners with all-electric heat pumps, plus HVAC contractors who buy its Redwood ducted unit
problem: Heat pump installs are expensive and fragmented, with slow quotes and many subcontractors. Electric Air runs its own crews with software driven quoting to cut cost.
business_model: Licensed contractor selling installs at fixed prices; also sells a ducted heat pump to contractors
product_category: Residential HVAC and heat pump installation (climate tech)

founders.name: Jeremy Osborne
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a renewable energy engineer with over a decade on heat pump systems.

founders.name: Chris Mui
founders.background_notes: Source: Attack Capital investment post, March 2023.

competitors.name: Elephant Energy
competitors.what: Heat pump and electrification installer, Colorado

technical_complexity.rationale: Installation business using off the shelf equipment; the hard parts are operations, permitting and quote software.

defensibility.rationale: Local contractor model with a state licence is copyable by other well funded installers; advantage rests on cost and execution.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it as of the sources checked; it kept operating with 600+ installs claimed on its site.

market_need_then: Gas furnace replacement and electrification incentives in California and US federal rebates in 2023 created demand; the company cites a $53B annual US market (company claim).

identity.voice_and_tone: Accountability and fixed pricing; one company handles everything.

branding.brand_signature: Redwood ducted heat pump product name
branding.community_and_virality: Company site cites a 5.0 rating from 100+ Google reviews.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; local reviews are positive but the brand is regional.

outcome_analysis: Electric Air is an active Bay Area heat pump contractor that joined YC in Summer 2023. The company site claims 600+ installs and a licensed contractor status. Funding detail is thin, so how far it has raised is not established, and well funded rivals like Quilt and Jetson entered the same market.
notes: Aggregators say about $500K total (YC and Leap Forward Ventures) and one says over $3M; both unverified so not recorded as rounds. The Attack Capital post confirms an investment in March 2023 but gives no amount. Elephant Energy source is dated 2026 though the seed was in 2022. Quilt (Redwood City) is a different company. A YC launch page mentions a Helios founder; not listed as a co-founder here.
